issues.title: Keyspace-set failures now discard the connection instead of keeping it silently wrong
issues.verdictReason: This is the PR's stated purpose (commit 7f48315d): previously a failed `use_keyspace()` was swallowed and the connection kept in the pool with the wrong keyspace (a real correctness bug); now it is discarded and the pool keeps retrying with backoff via need_filling()/refill_delay_strategy, it is not 'impossible to refill' — it will succeed again once the keyspace becomes valid, exactly as asserted by the new test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill.
issues.scopeReason: The behavior is new code added by this PR, even though it is working as intended rather than a defect.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A keyspace that fails USE every time now makes the pool impossible to refill; a failed Session::use_keyspace("typo") leaves the bad keyspace set and the PR discards every new connection instead of keeping it as before.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: A keyspace that fails USE every time now makes the pool impossible to refill; a failed Session::use_keyspace("typo") leaves the bad keyspace set and the PR discards every new connection instead of keeping it as before.

issues.title: Keyspace-failure handler doesn't check the failure is still for the current keyspace
issues.verdictReason: In handle_ready_connection's Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm (connection_pool.rs:900-911), the code unconditionally sets had_error_since_last_refill and can call update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())) without checking whether evt still matches self.current_keyspace; if use_keyspace() was called again in the meantime (self.current_keyspace changed), a stale error for the old keyspace can still raise backoff and publish a Broken state attributable to the superseded keyspace.
issues.scopeReason: This whole error arm, and the state side effects it triggers, were added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The keyspace-failure arm doesn't check whether the failed USE was for the current keyspace; a failure for a keyspace that has since been replaced still discards the connection, raises the backoff and can publish a stale Broken error.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: The keyspace-failure arm doesn't check whether the failed USE was for the current keyspace; a failure for a keyspace that has since been replaced still discards the connection, raises the backoff and can publish a stale Broken error.

issues.title: Excess shard-aware connection dropped on fallback retry without dec_total_connections
issues.verdictReason: In the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` branch (connection_pool.rs:994-1006), the already-opened `connection` is simply dropped (no connection_errors registration, no excess_connections push) after count_in_metrics already called inc_total_connections for it in start_opening_connection; there is no corresponding dec_total_connections, so total_connections leaks upward permanently for this path.
issues.scopeReason: `git diff main...HEAD` shows this branch byte-for-byte unchanged from main; it is pre-existing and not touched or made reachable by this PR, even though it is the same bug class the PR fixes elsewhere.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The commit that balances total_connections when clearing pools leaves out a sibling drop path: an excess shard-aware connection in the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` branch is dropped without dec_total_connections, even though count_in_metrics already incremented the metric for it.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: The commit that balances total_connections when clearing pools leaves out a sibling drop path: an excess shard-aware connection in the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` branch is dropped without dec_total_connections, even though count_in_metrics already incremented the metric for it.

issues.title: Stale ready_connections/keyspace comments no longer match the new failure path
issues.verdictReason: The field comment at connection_pool.rs:531-532 ('after its keyspace was correctly set') and the inline comment at connection_pool.rs:918-922 ('finally put into the conns') both describe the pre-PR behavior where a keyspace-set attempt always eventually produced a successful, pool-bound connection; the PR adds an Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace) path (connection_pool.rs:900) that discards the connection instead, which these comments do not mention.
issues.scopeReason: The PR's own new keyspace-failure branch is what makes these pre-existing comments inaccurate.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Comments still say ready_connections carries only connections whose keyspace was 'correctly set', and that a connection sent for keyspace setup will be 'finally put into the conns'. Both are now false.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: Comments still say ready_connections carries only connections whose keyspace was 'correctly set', and that a connection sent for keyspace setup will be 'finally put into the conns'. Both are now false.

issues.title: start_setting_keyspace_for_connection's doc comment no longer reflects that it can now…
issues.verdictReason: The comment 'Requires that the event is for a successful connection' above start_setting_keyspace_for_connection (connection_pool.rs:1328-1330) predates the PR, but previously the function's pushed future always resolved to Ok(...); after this PR it maps a failed use_keyspace() to Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) (connection_pool.rs:1341-1345), so the comment no longer conveys that the awaited event can now represent failure.
issues.scopeReason: The PR's change to this function's return value is what invalidates the comment's implicit guarantee.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The comment above start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, 'Requires that the event is for a successful connection', is now stale. The function takes a Connection, not an event, and its result can now be an Err event.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: The comment above start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, 'Requires that the event is for a successful connection', is now stale. The function takes a Connection, not an event, and its result can now be an Err event.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: One of the new keyspace tests finishes the proxy before dropping the refiller, the reverse of the sibling tests, and so has to whitelist DriverDisconnected.
